notes: Sixth sweep (2026-10-23, result.json head d04061d, uncommitted false): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). All have rc 0 and a model_id matching the requested model; every assistant message in each transcript names that model (the string claude-opus-5-5 in the haiku and sonnet transcripts sits only in the api-request-shape metadata record). reads is empty in all five, and each transcript shows a single Write call, no Skill, Read or Bash call.

git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes two of the eleven listed rules and one sentence of ex_unit.md (Capture logs, not in this case). The nine rules listed before are unchanged and are graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-22-d/grades/library-client-baseline.json: an option value passed to Req unchecked (and an API key checked only for truthiness or not at all) violates Make polymorphism explicit; options not checked with Keyword.validate!/2 or ## Options outside the function's @doc count against Group related parameters; an API key held in a Req request inside a package struct with no Inspect handling is violated, and a key never stored in a struct the package defines is not exercised; a public @doc false function without @spec violates Add specs, and message/1 under @impl needs none.

Read required keys (changed, newly indexed for this case): the sentence that decides the verdict here is "A pattern in a body that pulls one atom key or struct field out of a value the function already holds, with no literal and no guard, is dot access written long." As in evals/sweeps/2026-10-23-check/grades/library-client-skill.json, the rule names maps and structs, so Keyword.get on opts and settings[:key] on the keyword list haiku-2 builds (lines 73, 80, 86) are outside it. Case bullet 1 (re-match of a held value): 0 of 5 runs violated. Exercised by 1 of 5: opus-1 reads its client's fields with dot access (line 163: client.req; line 167: headers: [{"x-api-key", client.api_key}]). The other four have no body that reads a field of a value it holds (haiku-1 and haiku-2 pass loose values; sonnet-1 pipes the bare Req request; sonnet-2 takes :req in a single-clause head, line 61). Every run reads the required response keys with head patterns, so the rule's verdict is clean in all five.

In multi-clause functions (changed, newly indexed for this case): the sentence that decides the verdict is "A field no pattern or guard in the clause uses, bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, or bound in a head whose pattern `mix format` spreads over several lines, makes the reader scan every head to find what selects." Case bullet 2 (clutter): 0 of 5 runs violated. The three-or-more-clauses part was exercised by 4 of 5: handle_response/1 has three clauses in opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and binds body (and status) body-only in both Req.Response heads, but the third head is {:error, exception}, which binds no field, so no field is bound in every clause; opus-1's Error.message/1 has four clauses binding status, status and api_message, status and body, exception. haiku-1 has no such function (handle_response/1 has two clauses; decode/1 has three but binds the whole argument). The spread part was exercised by 3 of 5 and met: opus-1 parse_forecast/2 (lines 197-201), haiku-2 parse_forecast/1 (lines 104-109) and sonnet-2 Forecast.from_map/1 (lines 102-107) spread their first head while binding only keys the guard reads; sonnet-1's line 109, which mix format wraps only to move the guard, is the allowed form.

As in the check batch, "bound in every clause" is read as the same field in every clause. Under the reading where every head binds some body-only field, 1 of 5 runs would be violated: opus-1 Error.message/1 (line 47: def message(%__MODULE__{reason: :http_error, status: status, api_message: nil}) do; line 51 binds status and api_message; line 55 status and body; line 59: def message(%__MODULE__{reason: :transport_error, exception: exception}) do). The rule should say which reading it means; I would state "the same field", since that is how both grades of this rule's new text have read it.

Unchanged rules, judgement calls. Group related parameters, opus-1: options are checked with Keyword.validate/2 and a hand-written ArgumentError (lines 214-224) instead of Keyword.validate!/2, with a comment saying the bang version would put the API key in its message. That is true (Keyword.validate!([api_key: "SECRET", foo: 1], [:api_key]) raises "unknown keys [:foo] in [api_key: \"SECRET\", foo: 1], ..."), so the run checks its options as the rule asks and is clean. Use exception structs, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2: the @doc false Forecast parsers return a bare :error (sonnet-1 line 21, sonnet-2 line 111), which handle_response/1 turns into a WeatherClient.Error before any caller sees it; a bare :error carries no reason, unlike the {:error, :atom} the check batch counted, so both are clean. Keep secrets, sonnet-1: new/1 returns the bare Req request (line 75: @type t :: Req.Request.t()), so the verdict is not exercised and the inspect check is missed, as for the d sweep's sonnet-1.

Tier results that differ from the 2026-10-22-d baseline sweep come from the runs, not the rules: Opus is now clean on Make polymorphism explicit (every option value checked, lines 138-141) and on Add specs (no public @doc false function without a @spec); Haiku stays violated on Use exception structs, now through haiku-2 alone (tagged tuples); haiku-1 uses a defexception this time, where the d sweep's haiku-1 used a plain defstruct.

Other violations follow the previous standard: Before you finish where the file fails mix format --check-formatted (opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2; haiku-2 passes; confirmed in the scratch folder, matching result.json format_ok); a one-step with (haiku-1 line 73, haiku-2 line 91); a `_ ->` after {:ok, data} when is_map(data) that hides Jason's error, and a non-binary key reported as missing (haiku-1, haiku-2); an Error doc that defines the HTTP reason as 4xx/5xx while every non-2xx status lands there (sonnet-1, sonnet-2); a pipeline that starts with Req.new( (sonnet-2); an iex> example that makes a live request and cannot run as a doctest (haiku-2).

Compile results come from result.json and are not graded. opus-1 and sonnet-1 compile, with warnings only for the absent Req. haiku-1 and sonnet-2 do not compile because WeatherClient builds %Error{} before the file defines WeatherClient.Error; haiku-2 does not because WeatherClient builds %Forecast{} before defining WeatherClient.Forecast.
